"""Calendar date validation. Accepts only real calendar dates written YYYY-MM-DD."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from datetime import date

_SHAPE = re.compile(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}")


def check_date(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` when it is a real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form; otherwise raise ``ValueError``."""
    if not _SHAPE.fullmatch(text):
        raise ValueError(f"date must be written YYYY-MM-DD: {text!r}")
    try:
        date.fromisoformat(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"not a calendar date: {text!r}") from exc
    return text
----
"""Date validation: only real calendar dates written YYYY-MM-DD are accepted."""

import pytest

from cli.dates import check_date


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text",
    [
        "2026-01-01",
        "2024-02-29",
        "2026-12-31",
        "2000-02-29",
        "2026-04-30",
        "0001-01-01",
        "9999-12-31",
    ],
)
def test_real_calendar_date_is_returned_unchanged(text: str) -> None:
    assert check_date(text) == text


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text",
    [
        "2026-02-30",
        "2025-02-29",
        "1900-02-29",
        "2100-02-29",
        "2026-13-01",
        "2026-00-10",
        "2026-04-31",
        "2026-01-00",
        "0000-01-01",
    ],
)
def test_impossible_calendar_date_is_rejected(text: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        check_date(text)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text",
    [
        "2026-1-01",
        "2026-01-1",
        "26-01-01",
        "2026/01/01",
        "20260101",
        "01-01-2026",
        "2026-01-01 ",
        " 2026-01-01",
        "2026-01-01T00:00",
        "+026-01-01",
        "２０２６-01-01",
        "",
    ],
)
def test_malformed_shape_is_rejected(text: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        check_date(text)

"""Command-line entry point. ``main`` returns an exit status; it never exits the process."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys

from cli import commands
from cli.parser import UsageError, build_parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    try:
        args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    except UsageError as exc:
        # A usage error is one diagnostic line on standard error, with exit status 2.
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    except SystemExit as exc:
        # argparse exits 0 after printing --help to standard output.
        return int(exc.code or 0)
    return commands.dispatch(args)
